name: Tour de France
hook: Cycling's biggest race — yellow jerseys, the Champs-Élysées, and the Americans who defined it.

facts.label: Henri Desgrange
facts.statement: Henri Desgrange founded the race, first run in 1903, and created the maillot jaune, first worn by Eugène Christophe.

facts.label: the yellow jersey
facts.statement: The overall leader wears the maillot jaune, a yellow jersey, and the race winner receives one.

facts.label: the Champs-Élysées
facts.statement: The Tour traditionally finishes on the Champs-Élysées in Paris; since 1975 the finale has been an eight-lap circuit of the avenue.

facts.label: Greg LeMond
facts.statement: Greg LeMond, the American whose surname sounds French, won in 1986, 1989 and 1990.

facts.label: Lance Armstrong
facts.statement: Lance Armstrong won seven straight Tours from 1999 after beating cancer, then admitted doping to Oprah Winfrey in 2013 and lost the titles.

facts.label: Miguel Induráin
facts.statement: Spain's Miguel Induráin won five straight Tours from 1991 to 1995, a record.

facts.label: the Alps and the Pyrenees
facts.statement: The decisive climbing is in the Alps and the Pyrenees, including Alpine passes named for St. Bernard.
